title: Define a JPA entity with a generated primary key
question: Create a Product entity with an auto-generated ID, name, and price.
explanation: Use @Entity to map a class to a table, @Id for its primary key, and @GeneratedValue for ID generation. BigDecimal is preferred over double for monetary values.

title: Create a Spring Data JPA repository
question: Create a repository for Product entities with Long IDs and inherit CRUD operations.
answer:
public interface ProductRepository extends JpaRepository<Product, Long> {
}
explanation: JpaRepository provides common persistence operations such as save, findById, findAll, and deleteById. Add the Spring Data JPA starter and configure a datasource.

title: Write a derived query method
question: Write a repository method to find products whose names contain a phrase, ignoring case.
explanation: Spring Data parses the method name and creates a query. The property name must match the entity field; query cost depends on database indexes and matching strategy.

title: Find records with multiple conditions
question: Find active products in a price range using a derived repository method.
explanation: Derived methods support boolean predicates, comparisons, and combinations such as And and Or. Ensure the named properties exist on the entity.

title: Write a JPQL query with @Query
question: Use JPQL to find products priced below a supplied maximum.
explanation: JPQL refers to entity names and Java attributes rather than physical table and column names. Named parameters improve readability and avoid positional mistakes.

title: Write a native SQL query
question: Use a native SQL query to select products by an exact name.
explanation: Native queries use database SQL and physical table/column names, so they are less portable than JPQL. Adjust the table name to match your schema.

title: Implement pagination and sorting
question: Return one page of products sorted by price in ascending order.
explanation: Page numbers are zero-based. Validate page and size values and limit the maximum page size when they come from an API request.

title: Create a one-to-many relationship
question: Map one Customer to many Orders with the customer foreign key stored in the orders table.
explanation: The many-to-one side owns the foreign key. Keep both sides of a bidirectional relationship synchronized in helper methods; choose cascade behavior intentionally.

title: Map a many-to-many relationship
question: Map students and courses using a join table.
explanation: The owning side defines @JoinTable; the inverse side uses mappedBy. If the relationship has attributes of its own, model the join table as a separate entity instead.

title: Use @Embedded and @Embeddable for value objects
question: Map an Address value object inside a Customer table without creating a separate address entity.
explanation: An embeddable's fields are stored as columns in the owning entity's table by default. Use @AttributeOverrides if column names need customization.

title: Implement optimistic locking with @Version
question: Add optimistic locking to an entity to detect concurrent updates.
explanation: JPA checks the version during update and increments it when appropriate. Concurrent stale updates can raise an optimistic locking exception; handle conflicts at the service/API layer.

title: Run a service method inside a transaction
question: Load an entity, update a field, and persist the change transactionally.
explanation: A managed entity's changed fields are detected by dirty checking. Spring's transaction proxy applies transaction behavior when the method is invoked through the proxy.

title: Use a modifying query to update rows
question: Write a bulk JPQL update that changes a product's active flag by ID.
explanation: Bulk updates bypass normal entity dirty checking and can leave already-managed entities stale. Clearing the persistence context helps avoid reading outdated managed state.

title: Delete entities by a condition
question: Create a repository method to delete all expired sessions before a given timestamp.
explanation: Spring Data derives a delete query from the method name. The exact return type supported can depend on the method form and Spring Data version; verify it against your chosen version.

title: Avoid N+1 selects with EntityGraph
question: Load orders and their customer in a query method without triggering a separate customer lookup for every order.
explanation: An entity graph requests that the specified association be fetched for this operation. Inspect generated SQL and results because fetch behavior depends on provider and query shape.

title: Use a projection to return selected columns
question: Return only product ID and name using a Spring Data interface projection.
explanation: Interface projections can reduce unnecessary entity materialization and data transfer when only a subset of fields is needed. Getter names should match entity properties.

title: Implement an enum field with @Enumerated
question: Persist an order status as its enum name rather than its ordinal number.
explanation: EnumType.STRING stores values such as PAID and avoids ordinal shifts when enum constants are reordered. Renaming enum constants may require a data migration.

title: Use auditing fields for creation and modification times
question: Automatically populate createdAt and updatedAt timestamps using Spring Data JPA auditing.
explanation: Add the relevant Spring Data auditing imports and enable auditing. Auditing fields are populated during persistence lifecycle events; configure a DateTimeProvider if needed.

title: Write a repository test with @DataJpaTest
question: Test that a Product can be saved and retrieved using a JPA slice test.
explanation: @DataJpaTest configures a focused JPA test context and commonly uses an embedded database when available. Add suitable test dependencies and adapt entity constructors/accessors to your project.

title: Map a one-to-one relationship
question: Map a User entity to one Profile entity using a foreign key on the profile table.
explanation: The unique foreign key enforces that each profile references at most one user. Lazy loading for one-to-one associations can vary by provider and mapping details, so verify behavior with your JPA implementation.
